newsitem.title: USA: Pittsburgh bracing for Ku Klux Klan rally.
newsitem.headline: Pittsburgh bracing for Ku Klux Klan rally.

text.p: City officials and police said Thursday they planned extensive security measures for a Ku Klux Klan rally scheduled for Saturday on the steps of a downtown city government building.

More than 200 police were assigned to the rally and a 4-foot-high fence will be constructed around the area where Klan members will speak. There will also be a fence around the area directly across the street where the audience will stand.
Peg McCormick, a spokeswoman for Pittsburgh Mayor Tom Murphy, said the fences were intended "to protect everybody."

"We are not a hate group," said Jeff Berry, National Imperial Wizard of the KKK. "We do not go into these states to rally and to start hate. It's usually the protesters ... that are the ones who get arrested."
A federal judge ruled last month that stopping the rally would violate the First Amendment. The white supremacist group had sued after the city denied them a permit to demonstrate.

Brad Thompson, second in the Klan's national hierarchy, said he expected more than 2,000 people at the event. He said there would be about 50 Klan members on the building steps and about 100 to 150 supporters in the audience, with supporters were coming from New York, Ohio, Illinois and Indiana.
A group of community activists said they would hold a counter-rally across the street.
